cards.explanation: The answer is True. The LORD says, "For I have chosen him, so that he will command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing what is right and just…" (Genesis 18:19). So Abraham's chosen to hand something down, and it starts at home. I like that, friends. The best recipes get passed down the same way, standing at the counter.

The answer is that He will go down and see if their actions fit the outcry. The LORD says, "I will go down to see if their actions fully justify the outcry that has reached Me. If not, I will find out." (Genesis 18:21). He says He will go down and see. Nobody rushes this one, friends, and I think that matters.

The answer is, "Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?" (Genesis 18:23). Abraham steps forward to say it, too. Notice he doesn't ask to be let off, friends. He asks about the righteous people who might be in that city.

The answer is the Judge of all the earth. Abraham says, "Will not the Judge of all the earth do what is right?" (Genesis 18:25). Think about why that title fits, friends. He's asking about judging, so he calls the LORD the Judge. He also says, "Far be it from You…" twice, which tells me he means every word.

The answer is spare. The LORD says, "If I find fifty righteous ones within the city of Sodom, on their account I will spare the whole place." (Genesis 18:26). Spare the WHOLE place, mind you, friends. Abraham asked about fifty righteous people, and the answer covers everybody else there too.

The answer is True. Abraham asks, "…suppose the fifty righteous ones lack five. Will You destroy the whole city for the lack of five?" and the LORD replies, "If I find forty-five there, I will not destroy it." (Genesis 18:28). Five short, and the answer is still no destruction, friends. Abraham is just getting warmed up.

The answer is False. Abraham asks, "Suppose thirty are found there?" and the LORD replies, "If I find thirty there, I will not do it." (Genesis 18:30). He says thirty is enough, friends, not that it falls short. Abraham asked and the answer was yes again.

The answer is twenty. Abraham says, "Now that I have ventured to speak to the Lord, suppose twenty are found there?" (Genesis 18:31). Each time he asks, the number drops, friends. And each time, the answer is the same: no destruction. The LORD answers, "On account of the twenty, I will not destroy it."

The answer is ten. Abraham says, "May the Lord not be angry, but let me speak once more. Suppose ten are found there?" (Genesis 18:32). And the LORD answers, "On account of the ten, I will not destroy it." Ten is where Abraham stops asking, friends.

The answer is that the LORD departs and Abraham returns home. "When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed, and Abraham returned home." (Genesis 18:33). The conversation ends, and Abraham goes back home, friends. The text doesn't say what Abraham was thinking on that walk. I'd bet it was a quiet one. And the story isn't over.
